sections.label: sec:foundations-endpoints
sections.content: Definitions of closed topological and smooth three-manifold, simple connectedness including nonemptiness, based cube homotopy groups, standard unit S3, and both universal endpoints.
hypotheses_checked: IsManifold R3 infinity only for smooth endpoint
sections.alignment: Initial topology proposition records finite dimension and all-basepoint homotopy consequences proved by supporting theorems. The public M02 record stores an actual CW structure, one selected basepoint and its groups, orientation, and an unbased homotopy equivalence. Its signature is not being strengthened or edited.

sections.label: sec:foundations-triangulation
sections.content: Finite smooth embedding, uniform graph charts and tubular projection, finite-candidate slab avoidance, join-distance induction, active-face order complex, coherent section centers and normal-fiber contraction.
hypotheses_checked: mesh lies within actual nearest-projection neighborhood
sections.mechanism: At most m(m+1)^(N-1) of (m+1)^N candidate points lie in forbidden slabs. The join inequality max(at,d-aD) >= dt/(D+t) propagates clearance. Active face cardinalities N-2 through N+1 bound chains by four. Center coordinates and altitudes yield Lip(E) <= C_N epsilon <= 1/2. Solve v=-P_T E(v) to obtain exactly one point per normal fiber; compact-to-Hausdorff bijection gives the homeomorphism.
sections.depth_note: Expanded after author audit: supporting hyperplane reduction and opposite-ray construction give a minimal section through each vertex; a normal-space ball bounds the affine inverse and makes the graph equation contractive. Coning convex sections explains the tangent flag carrier. Exclusive-coordinate elimination derives the factor (1+eta^-1)^k-1, and altitude bounds turn it into a displacement estimate. Independent calibration/source review remains required; author expansion is not an acceptance verdict.

sections.label: sec:foundations-orientation
sections.content: Two independent orientation-cover constructions, using determinant signs and local integral homology frames.
sections.mechanism: Chain-rule determinant cocycle and separately excision/localization frames define discrete two-sheeted covers. Simply connected covering lift yields sections, hence locally constant chart signs and locally represented local generators. Their chosen global signs are not silently identified.

sections.label: sec:foundations-top-homology
sections.content: Compact-support detection/gluing, locally constant coefficients of top classes, and the fundamental class.
sections.mechanism: Compact relative supports reduce to finite unions of balls and relative Mayer-Vietoris. Localize a-c(p)b to prove the coefficient function locally constant. Connectedness and support detection make evaluation injective; the glued class with coefficient one makes it surjective.

sections.label: sec:foundations-second-homology
sections.content: Compact-support cap maps, four-clause open-set invariant, union diagram chase, chart boxes and directed limits, finite chart-cover induction, and direct vanishing of H1 cohomology.
hypotheses_checked: Coherent integral orientation on ambient manifold
D1 epi, D2/D3 iso, all Hc^q vanish q>=4
Induction retains every open W contained in a finite chart union
Compactness identifies Hc1 with H1 cohomology
Simply connected paths make every singular one-cocycle a coboundary
sections.mechanism: Lift the homology boundary using D2 on the intersection; use injectivity on U,V and exactness to obtain a cohomology lift; remove the residual using D1 on U,V. Five-lemma/cokernel arguments preserve D2,D3 and high-degree vanishing. Integrating a cocycle along chosen paths gives a vertex zero-cochain. Hc1=0 and D1 surjective imply H2=0.
sections.alignment: The construction proves the four needed cap clauses, not an assumed general duality service. The arbitrary-universe adapter changes carrier through an actual finite-complex homeomorphism; the small-carrier core is topological.

sections.label: sec:foundations-hurewicz
sections.content: Integral Hurewicz in degrees two and three, explicit connectivity checks and choice of nonzero generator.
sections.mechanism: Coherent simplex straightening and prism chains explain the implemented Hurewicz maps. First pi1=0 gives pi2=H2=0; then pi1=pi2=0 gives pi3=H3=Z at every basepoint.

sections.label: sec:foundations-cw-equivalence
sections.content: Constructing an actual inverse for a generator sphere map by contracting the two-skeleton inclusion, relative extension over three-cells, and cancellation on pi3.
sections.mechanism: Choose a zero-cell and generator f. Nullhomotope inclusion of the two-skeleton inside C, extend to a map a homotopic to id and constant on that skeleton, lift its three-cell maps through f_*, and paste g. Obtain fg~id relative to the basepoint; injectivity of f_* then gives gf~id. No claim that the two-skeleton itself is contractible.
sections.alignment: The stronger field has real later consumers in M57 free sphere nullhomotopy and selected surgery comparison homotopy equivalence, separately from initial width nontriviality.

sections.label: sec:foundations-projective-plane
sections.content: Exact excluded open product neighborhood and orientation-reversing deck contradiction.
hypotheses_checked: Proposed embedding merely topological and open
sections.mechanism: Correct signs by reflection; pull charts back with transition cancellation, not differentiation of the embedding. Positive derivative gives local generator preservation. Lift to S2 x (-1,1), identify it with shell by (u,t)->(2+t)u, and calculate deck sign using cover-swap Mayer-Vietoris, punctured-pair boundary and translations. The comparison sign is constant on the connected cover, contradicting deck invariance.

findings.finding: The original normal-fiber conclusion identifies images under F, but injectivity of the abstract flag realization was not established in the prose.
findings.correction: Positive ambient coordinates identify the largest face; the minimum ratio to its center recovers that flag coefficient. Repeated subtraction determines the entire flag and proves F injective.

findings.finding: Coning a convex polytope alone did not explain why the prescribed active-face centers give the exact subdivision used by the comparison map.
findings.correction: The coordinate constraints characterize section vertices. The minimum coordinate ratio yields z = a*c + (1-a)*y with strictly smaller support for y. Support induction proves coverage with the prescribed centers, and the coefficient uniqueness proves the face intersections. The 4Lh tangent disk is covered because every containing simplex lies within 6Lh.

findings.finding: The claim that every global normal-fiber point is captured by the local comparison omitted the geometric containment and the actual comparison preimage.
findings.correction: A global carrier point is within 2Lh of its nearest manifold point. Its largest ambient face is therefore within 4Lh. Replacing graph centers by tangent centers with the same convex coefficients gives an actual preimage in the contraction disk. Normal-fiber uniqueness and global F injectivity then give injectivity of nu composed with F.

findings.finding: Uniqueness of a fixed point on the normal ball was used as uniqueness in the full face without explicitly checking that every graph intersection belongs to that ball.
findings.correction: The graph error bounds the normal coordinate of every intersection by epsilon*R, and the uniform chart covers every manifold point of the face. Thus every intersection is a fixed point of the same contraction.

findings.finding: The enlargement from a compact support to a union of balls did not say why vanishing at the original support forces vanishing on the larger support.
findings.correction: Choose the balls centered on the original support. Restriction to the local group at each center is an isomorphism for that ball; detection on the union then proves the claim. Display the gluing exact sequence and the H4 vanishing that gives uniqueness, defining support homology in every degree.
findings.source: Hatcher, Lemma 3.27, proof steps (1)-(4), pp. 237-238; PoincareLib/AlgebraicTopology/SingularHomology/Relative/IntegralCompactGluing.lean:integralCompactSupport_local_to_global and exists_unique_integralSupportHomology_compact_gluing

checked_without_further_expansion.result: Supporting-plane reduction gives at most d projected vertices at the opposite-ray endpoint; the small-face gap forces exactly d+1 vertices after adjoining the prescribed vertex. The inverse norm is bounded by diameter/a, so the same-face graph displacement is at most 24*L^2*epsilon*h/b.

Exclusive-coordinate elimination satisfies A_k = eta^-1 + (1+eta^-1)*A_(k-1), A_0=0, hence A_k=(1+eta^-1)^k-1. The altitude h/4 and k<=4 give exactly C_N=96*L^2/b*((1+eta^-1)^4-1). Convex disk segmentation gives the global Lipschitz bound, with epsilon chosen before h. No constant or quantifier correction is required.

Coherent local generators yield top homology by compact gluing and locally constant coefficients. The four-clause cap property closes under unions and chart exhaustion; the chosen-path one-cocycle primitive kills Hc1 on compact M. Hurewicz is used only in degrees two then three with connectivity proved. The cellular construction contracts the inclusion of the two-skeleton, pastes relative three-cell lifts, and cancels postcomposition on based pi3.

The proposed embedding is only topological. Pulling back the positive atlas cancels it from transition maps; no derivative of the embedding is used. The lifted orientation is deck-invariant, whereas the connected shell comparison makes the deck transformation reverse every orientation. Compactness and simple connectedness are not assumptions of the obstruction.
